newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Mubarak returns home after talks in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak returns home after talks in Syria.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak returned to Cairo on Saturday from Syria, where he held talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad on the Middle East peace process.
An airport source reported Mubarak's return to the Egyptian capital from Damascus, where Syrian presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said the two leaders held first a closed-door meeting.
They were later joined by Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam, Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, Egyptian presidential adviser Osama al-Baz and Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.

The official Syrian News Agency (SANA) quoted Egyptian Information Minister Safwat al-Sherif as saying Arab leaders need to meet to evaluate developments on the Syrian-Israeli track of the peace process.
"The developments require such meetings to evaluate the peace process on the Syrian track and to evaluate the commitment to the (peace) agreements," Sharif added.
Moussa held talks on Friday with European Union envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos about the Syrian and Lebanese tracks of the peace process between Israel and its Arab neighbours.
Moussa had said Egypt, Syria and Saudi Arabia were coordinating on ways to boost negotiations.
Khaddam and Shara toured several Arab countries, including Egypt and Saudi Arabia, over the past month to garner support for Damascus in its deadlocked talks with Israel.
Talks between Syria and Israel were halted last year while the Jewish state still had a Labour government in office.
The main stumbling block in the negotiations were the Golan Heights, which Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war.
Negotiations have not resumed under right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who rejects trading occupied Arab land for peace.
Syria says the former Israeli government had agreed to return the Golan and insists it will resume talks with Israel if they begin where the last round left off.
